name: cnspy trajectory evaluation
summary: Python package that aligns an estimated trajectory with ground truth from CSV files, associates timestamps and reports position/attitude error metrics, including NEES from pose covariance.
why_it_matters: Consistency checks (NEES) matter as much as RMSE when judging a GNSS-denied filter; this tool computes both from plain CSV.
hackathon_notes: pip install cnspy-trajectory-evaluation; estimated CSV must carry pose covariance. Use evo for quick plots, this when you need filter consistency.

name: GTSfM
summary: End-to-end structure-from-motion pipeline built on GTSAM, with pluggable front-ends (classical and learned matchers) and distributed execution via Dask.
why_it_matters: Builds georeferenceable 3D maps from drone or ground imagery, which can serve as prior maps for visual localization.
hackathon_notes: Conda environment install; runs on image folders or COLMAP-format data. Expect long runtimes on large sets - downsample.

name: CANboat
summary: Toolkit for NMEA 2000 networks: a PGN decoder/analyzer plus utilities to read, write and convert N2K and NMEA 0183 messages, used largely for reverse-engineering marine bus traffic.
why_it_matters: Gives raw access to ship sensor buses (GNSS, heading, AIS, depth), useful for maritime nav integrity monitoring and spoofing detection research.
hackathon_notes: Build analyzer and pipe candump/actisense logs through it to JSON. Needs a CAN or N2K gateway for live data; sample logs work offline.

name: Beluga
summary: Modern C++17 library of Monte Carlo Localization algorithms with a ROS 2 node that is a drop-in replacement for the Nav2 AMCL package.
why_it_matters: Map-based particle-filter localization for ground robots operating without GNSS; easier to extend than legacy AMCL.
hackathon_notes: Swap beluga_amcl for nav2_amcl in a Nav2 launch file; same parameters. Good base for adding custom sensor models.

name: Fraunhofer IIS Jammertest 2025 dataset
summary: Real-world GNSS interference recordings from Jammertest 2025 at Andoya, Norway, covering jamming, spoofing, meaconing and multi-emitter scenarios, with metadata for classification, characterization and direction finding.
why_it_matters: Rare open real-world interference data from live jamming trials, suited to training and testing interference detectors and classifiers.
hackathon_notes: Download the data and start with the provided Python loaders; pick one scenario class to build a jamming/spoofing classifier within a day.

name: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM (2nd ed.) code
summary: Companion code for the second edition of Gao Xiang's visual SLAM textbook: Lie groups, nonlinear optimization, feature VO, direct methods, back-end and loop closure examples in C++.
why_it_matters: One of the most-used hands-on routes into visual SLAM internals; good for bringing a team up to speed fast.
hackathon_notes: Each chapter builds standalone; dependency versions (Pangolin, Sophus, g2o) are old - use the bundled 3rdparty or a Docker image.

name: CU Boulder GNSS SDR Collection
summary: University of Colorado Boulder collection of MATLAB software-defined GNSS receiver code-bases, organized per constellation (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou), with linked sample data sets.
why_it_matters: Teaching-grade multi-constellation receivers you can read end to end, from acquisition to tracking and navigation.
hackathon_notes: Point the settings file at one of the provided IQ data sets and run. MATLAB licence required; slow on long recordings.

name: GVINS
summary: Tightly coupled GNSS-visual-inertial estimator that fuses raw GNSS pseudorange and Doppler with VIO in a factor graph, giving drift-free global poses and smooth local tracking.
why_it_matters: Shows how raw GNSS measurements degrade gracefully into VIO when satellites are blocked, a core pattern for contested or urban PNT.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 (Melodic/Noetic) only; run on the GVINS dataset bags. Porting to ROS 2 is non-trivial.

name: SLAM Toolbox (MATLAB)
summary: Joan Sola's MATLAB EKF-SLAM toolbox with landmark parameterizations (points, lines, inverse depth) and simulated or real sensor support, written for teaching and prototyping.
why_it_matters: Readable reference for EKF-SLAM landmark handling, by the author of the widely cited Lie theory and quaternion kinematics notes.
hackathon_notes: Runs in MATLAB with simulated worlds out of the box; not maintained, use for understanding rather than deployment.

name: fuse
summary: ROS framework for sensor fusion as factor-graph optimization: plugin sensor models, motion models and publishers on top of Ceres, supporting both smoothing and fixed-lag estimation.
why_it_matters: A more flexible alternative to robot_localization EKF when you need delayed measurements, robust losses or custom constraints.
hackathon_notes: Use the fuse tutorials or the ROSCon UK 2025 workshop Docker image; plugin config in YAML. Ceres dependency builds slowly.

name: ROSCon UK 2025 State Estimation workshop
summary: Materials for an eight-task ROS 2 state estimation workshop at ROSCon UK 2025, with a Docker image, recorded bags and step-by-step exercises using robot_localization and fuse.
why_it_matters: Ready-made, containerized curriculum for wiring wheel odometry, IMU and GNSS into a ROS 2 estimator.
hackathon_notes: docker compose run with the provided compose file; work through tasks in order. Fastest way to get a fused ROS 2 pose estimate running.

name: mil-sym-ts
summary: TypeScript/JavaScript renderer for MIL-STD-2525 (D and later) military symbology, producing single-point and multi-point tactical graphics for web maps.
why_it_matters: Standard-conformant symbols are the expected visual language for any common operational picture or C2 demo.
hackathon_notes: npm package; render SIDC codes to SVG/canvas and drop onto Leaflet/Cesium/OpenLayers layers. Multi-point graphics need control-point ordering per the standard.

name: MIT VNAV lab data
summary: Pointer repo for the ROS bag files used in MIT's Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles course exercises.
why_it_matters: Supplies the datasets that make the VNAV labs runnable outside MIT.
hackathon_notes: Only a README with a download link; fetch bags alongside VNAV-labs.

name: MIT VNAV labs
summary: Lab assignments for MIT 16.485 Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles: ROS, 3D geometry, trajectory optimization, feature tracking, two-view geometry, VIO and place recognition.
why_it_matters: A structured, graded path from ROS basics to visual-inertial navigation, built by the SPARK lab behind Kimera.
hackathon_notes: Labs assume Ubuntu + ROS; pick individual labs (feature tracking, two-view geometry) as warm-ups.

name: MoveIt 2
summary: Motion planning framework for ROS 2 manipulators: kinematics, collision checking, planners (OMPL, Pilz, STOMP) and real-time servoing.
why_it_matters: Relevant when a vehicle carries an arm or gimbal-like mechanism; outside pure navigation but the ROS 2 standard for manipulation planning.
hackathon_notes: Binary install via apt; use the MoveIt Setup Assistant for a new robot. Overkill unless your platform has an arm.

name: Jammertest test plan
summary: Official test catalog and plan for Jammertest, Norway's annual live GNSS jamming and spoofing event, maintained by the Norwegian Public Roads Administration.
why_it_matters: The reference for which interference scenarios were transmitted when, needed to label any Jammertest recording.
hackathon_notes: Use the per-year plan to map timestamps in Jammertest datasets to emitted scenarios.

name: Isaac ROS Visual SLAM
summary: ROS 2 package wrapping NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated cuVSLAM for stereo visual(-inertial) odometry and SLAM on Jetson and x86 GPUs.
why_it_matters: Real-time VIO on embedded Jetson hardware with low CPU load, a practical GNSS-denied odometry source for drones and UGVs.
hackathon_notes: Use the Isaac ROS dev container; RealSense or ZED stereo works out of the box. Jetson Orin recommended.

name: Nav2 tutorials
summary: Tutorial packages referenced by docs.nav2.org: example planner, controller and behavior-tree plugins, SLAM and GPS waypoint following setups.
why_it_matters: Shortest path to custom Nav2 plugins and GPS-based outdoor navigation in ROS 2.
hackathon_notes: Clone into a ROS 2 workspace matching your distro branch; the GPS waypoint follower demo runs in Gazebo.

name: SLAM Handbook (public release)
summary: Release repo for the SLAM Handbook (Cambridge University Press), edited by Carlone, Kim, Barfoot, Cremers and Dellaert, published incrementally in three parts from late 2024.
why_it_matters: Current, expert-written reference covering factor graphs through spatial AI; free drafts for the whole team.
hackathon_notes: Download chapter PDFs from the release page; factor-graph chapter is the best starting point.

name: VAARA Jammertest dataset
summary: University of Vaasa public GNSS dataset recorded at Jammertest 2024, released in batches from autumn 2025 under a Finland-NSF project on secure satellite navigation.
why_it_matters: Second independent real-world interference dataset, useful for cross-dataset validation of detectors.
hackathon_notes: Check README for which batches are released; pair with the Jammertest plan for labels.

name: STEAM
summary: Simultaneous Trajectory Estimation and Mapping engine from UTIAS: a C++ nonlinear least-squares library with continuous-time Gaussian-process trajectory priors on Lie groups.
why_it_matters: Continuous-time estimation handles asynchronous, motion-distorted sensors such as spinning radar and lidar.
hackathon_notes: Library, not an application; see steam_icp for a ready odometry pipeline built on it.

name: ROSA (ROS Agent)
summary: NASA JPL's LangChain-based AI agent that lets operators query and command ROS 1 and ROS 2 systems in natural language through a set of ROS introspection and control tools.
why_it_matters: A credible, lab-backed reference for putting an LLM in the loop of a robot stack, with tool boundaries an operator can audit.
hackathon_notes: pip install jpl-rosa; demo runs against turtlesim in Docker. Add custom tools for your MAVROS/Nav2 topics.

name: ROS MCP Server
summary: Model Context Protocol server that exposes ROS topics, services and parameters (via rosbridge) to LLM clients such as Claude or GPT, for ROS 1 and ROS 2.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to let an LLM inspect and drive an existing robot without changing robot code.
hackathon_notes: Run rosbridge on the robot and point the MCP client config at the server; works with sim (Gazebo/Isaac). Add safety limits before anything flies.

name: ROS MCP Server demos
summary: Demos and tutorials for connecting LLMs to robots via the ROS MCP server, including simulated mobile robots.
why_it_matters: Worked examples shorten the path from install to a talking robot demo.
hackathon_notes: Follow one demo end to end before customizing the server.

name: WiseVision ROS 2 MCP
summary: MCP server that lets AI agents discover and operate ROS 2 robots: topic echo/publish, services, actions and introspection, implemented natively in ROS 2 rather than through rosbridge.
why_it_matters: Native ROS 2 alternative for LLM control without a rosbridge hop.
hackathon_notes: Build in a ROS 2 workspace; check supported distros in README.

name: LCAS ROS 2 MCP
summary: ROS 2 MCP server from the Lincoln Centre for Autonomous Systems, exposing topics, services and actions to LLM agents.
why_it_matters: University-maintained option for agricultural/field robot agent experiments.
hackathon_notes: Smaller project; compare with ros-mcp-server before committing.

name: MAVLinkMCP
summary: MCP server bridging an LLM to a drone over MAVLink, exposing arming, takeoff, waypoint and telemetry tools via MAVSDK.
why_it_matters: Direct template for a natural-language drone mission interface on PX4/ArduPilot SITL.
hackathon_notes: Pair with PX4 or ArduPilot SITL; never point at a real vehicle without geofence and human confirm.

name: mavlink-mcp (ArduPilot)
summary: MCP server for flying ArduPilot vehicles from AI agents over MAVLink, covering missions, camera vision and SITL workflows.
why_it_matters: Another ready LLM-to-autopilot bridge, oriented to ArduPilot missions.
hackathon_notes: Young project; test thoroughly in SITL.

name: ardupilot-mcp (safety-gated)
summary: SITL-first MCP server for talking to ArduPilot vehicles over MAVLink, with explicit safety gating of commands.
why_it_matters: Its safety-gate design is a useful pattern for keeping an LLM from issuing unsafe flight commands.
hackathon_notes: Small codebase; read the gating logic and reuse it in your own bridge.

name: QGIS MCP
summary: MCP server plus QGIS plugin that lets an LLM create projects, load layers, run processing algorithms and execute PyQGIS code in QGIS Desktop.
why_it_matters: Natural-language GIS analysis for terrain, route and coverage products in a mission-planning demo.
hackathon_notes: Install the plugin, start the socket server in QGIS, add the MCP server to the client. Arbitrary code execution - sandbox it.

name: qgis-mcp (nkarasiak)
summary: Actively maintained MCP bridge connecting AI agents to QGIS Desktop, with a broader tool set than the original qgis_mcp.
why_it_matters: More recent alternative if the original QGIS MCP lags behind QGIS releases.
hackathon_notes: Same plugin-plus-server pattern; check QGIS version compatibility.

name: GIS MCP Server
summary: MCP server giving LLMs geospatial operations through Shapely, PyProj, GeoPandas and Rasterio: geometry ops, CRS transforms, distances and raster analysis, without a desktop GIS.
why_it_matters: Headless geodesy/GIS tool layer an agent can call for coordinate conversion and spatial reasoning.
hackathon_notes: pip install gis-mcp; no QGIS needed. Good for an agent that must reason about coordinates and areas.

name: LLM-Geo (Autonomous GIS)
summary: Research prototype of an LLM-driven 'autonomous GIS' that turns a spatial question into a solution graph, generates code and executes the analysis to return maps and numbers.
why_it_matters: Early worked example of LLM planning over geospatial workflows, a building block for agentic mission planning.
hackathon_notes: Notebook-driven; needs an LLM API key. Use as design reference rather than a dependency.

name: TypeFly
summary: Framework for LLM-based drone task planning that compiles natural-language requests into a compact robot language (MiniSpec) executed on a DJI Tello with vision services.
why_it_matters: Shows how to constrain LLM output into a small, verifiable command language for drones, cutting latency and risk.
hackathon_notes: Works with a cheap Tello and a GPU box for YOLO; virtual mode exists. Swap the backend for MAVSDK to target PX4.

name: PromptCraft-Robotics
summary: Microsoft's collection of prompts and an AirSim-based ChatGPT drone simulator accompanying the 'ChatGPT for Robotics' work.
why_it_matters: Classic starting point for prompting LLMs to produce drone control code in simulation.
hackathon_notes: No longer updated and AirSim itself is archived; mine the prompts, run elsewhere.

name: ROS-LLM
summary: Framework for natural-language interaction with ROS robots, letting an LLM call robot functions and chain behaviors.
why_it_matters: Earlier ROS-native LLM integration; useful comparison to MCP-based designs.
hackathon_notes: Not updated since 2023; prefer ROSA or the MCP servers for new work.

name: OpenFly
summary: Platform for outdoor aerial vision-language navigation: multi-engine simulators (UE, GTA V, Google Earth, 3DGS), automated data collection toolchain, a large benchmark and a keyframe-aware VLN model.
why_it_matters: Largest open aerial VLN benchmark, for agents that fly to places described in words.
hackathon_notes: Heavy downloads and GPU; use the released dataset with the baseline model rather than regenerating data.

name: AerialVLN
summary: Benchmark and simulator (AirSim/UE-based) for vision-and-language navigation by UAVs in city-scale environments, with baseline agents.
why_it_matters: The first widely used aerial VLN benchmark; baseline for language-commanded drone navigation.
hackathon_notes: Large simulator assets; plan download time. Linux + GPU.

name: CityNav
summary: Language-goal aerial navigation dataset over real-city 3D point clouds with geographic information, plus baselines that use map-based landmark grounding.
why_it_matters: Links language goals to real geography, close to how operators describe destinations.
hackathon_notes: Dataset plus training code; GPU needed for baselines.

name: SatNav
summary: Scalable benchmark and platform for long-horizon UAV vision-language navigation built from satellite imagery (NeurIPS 2026 Datasets track).
why_it_matters: Satellite-imagery grounding matches what a real UAV can carry as a prior map, so results transfer better to GNSS-denied ops.
hackathon_notes: New release; check README for data availability before planning around it.

name: 3DG-VLN
summary: UAV vision-language navigation framework using 3D grounding for more precise goal localization (2026 research code).
why_it_matters: Recent aerial VLN method to compare against benchmark baselines.
hackathon_notes: Research code; reproduce only if you need a SOTA aerial VLN baseline.

name: InternNav
summary: Open platform for building and evaluating generalist navigation foundation models, covering VLN and related embodied navigation tasks with training and benchmarks.
why_it_matters: Brings recent VLA-style navigation models into one toolkit.
hackathon_notes: Large models and simulators; use the provided checkpoints.

name: NaVid / Uni-NaVid
summary: Evaluation code for NaVid and Uni-NaVid, video-based VLMs that plan the next navigation step from monocular RGB history in continuous VLN environments.
why_it_matters: Shows map-free, camera-only language navigation, relevant when maps and GNSS are unavailable.
hackathon_notes: Requires Habitat and large checkpoints; evaluation only.

name: GNM / ViNT / NoMaD
summary: Code and checkpoints for general visual navigation foundation models (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD) that drive robots from camera images toward image goals or explore, with ROS deployment code.
why_it_matters: Pretrained camera-only navigation policies that run on small robots, a ready learned navigation baseline.
hackathon_notes: Deploy NoMaD on a Jetson-class robot with a fisheye camera; topological graph from a teleop run.

name: LM-Nav
summary: Code for LM-Nav, which composes a language model, CLIP and a visual navigation model to follow natural-language route instructions without language-annotated robot data.
why_it_matters: Early demonstration of building language navigation from off-the-shelf pretrained parts.
hackathon_notes: Mostly notebook-level; read for the architecture.

name: VLMaps
summary: Builds visual-language maps by fusing pretrained visual-language features into a 3D reconstruction, enabling open-vocabulary landmark navigation from natural language.
why_it_matters: Language-queryable maps are a natural interface for operators tasking robots.
hackathon_notes: Habitat-based data; GPU needed for feature extraction.

name: ConceptGraphs
summary: Builds open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs from RGB-D by associating 2D foundation-model detections across views, then lets an LLM plan over the graph.
why_it_matters: Object-level semantic maps an LLM can reason about, useful for tasking and situational awareness.
hackathon_notes: Heavy dependencies (SAM, CLIP, GroundingDINO); start from Replica examples.

name: NavGPT
summary: Purely LLM-based vision-and-language navigation agent that reasons explicitly over textual observations to choose actions (AAAI 2024).
why_it_matters: Readable baseline for LLM reasoning in navigation, with prompts you can adapt.
hackathon_notes: Needs an LLM API and R2R/Matterport data.

name: Co-NavGPT
summary: Multi-robot exploration and object search where an LLM assigns frontier goals to robots from a merged semantic map.
why_it_matters: LLM as a multi-agent tasker, a pattern for swarm search missions.
hackathon_notes: Habitat simulation; adapt the goal-assignment prompt for your own swarm sim.

name: IEZ (INS-EKF-ZUPT)
summary: MATLAB implementation of a foot-mounted INS with EKF and zero-velocity updates for pedestrian dead reckoning, with sample datasets from two foot-mounted MPU6050 IMUs.
why_it_matters: Compact reference for the standard ZUPT pedestrian tracker that underpins dismounted soldier navigation.
hackathon_notes: Runs offline on included data; reproduce with any cheap IMU strapped to a boot.

name: MPU6050 ZUPT
summary: Arduino/MPU6050 library implementing several open-source foot-mounted INS and zero-velocity detection algorithms.
why_it_matters: Low-cost hardware path to a working foot-mounted INS demo.
hackathon_notes: Needs an MPU6050 and microcontroller; expect heading drift without magnetometer aiding.

name: OpenPDR
summary: Device-independent pedestrian dead reckoning library: step detection, step length estimation and heading for smartphone-style sensors.
why_it_matters: Simple step-and-heading baseline for phone-based indoor navigation.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained since 2017; use for algorithm reference.

name: PDR Android app
summary: Android app implementing pedestrian dead reckoning with step detection and orientation from phone sensors.
why_it_matters: Phone-native PDR demo you can install and walk with during a hackathon.
hackathon_notes: Build with Android Studio; fuse with Wi-Fi or UWB for correction.

name: RIDI
summary: Code for RIDI, which regresses velocity from smartphone IMU data with learned models to reduce inertial drift for pedestrian navigation.
why_it_matters: Ancestor of RoNIN/TLIO-style learned inertial odometry.
hackathon_notes: Old dependencies; prefer RoNIN for new work.

name: Indoor Location Competition 2.0
summary: Data and baseline code from Microsoft Research's Indoor Location Competition 2.0: smartphone IMU, Wi-Fi, BLE and magnetic traces across many buildings with floor maps.
why_it_matters: Large real indoor dataset for Wi-Fi/magnetic fingerprinting plus PDR fusion.
hackathon_notes: Sample data in repo; full set on Kaggle. Good for a fingerprinting + PDR fusion demo.

name: MILUV devkit
summary: Python devkit for MILUV, a multi-UAV indoor localization dataset with UWB ranging (including inter-robot), vision and IMU data.
why_it_matters: UWB plus vision data with multiple vehicles, for relative and indoor localization.
hackathon_notes: Download the dataset via devkit scripts; examples include UWB EKF.

name: PVI polarization navigation dataset
summary: Dataset combining stereo camera, IMU, polarization camera and high-precision GPS for polarization-aided navigation research.
why_it_matters: Polarized skylight gives a GNSS-free heading reference; open data for it is rare.
hackathon_notes: README only links a Google Drive; check data format before planning.

name: celnav
summary: Python celestial navigation tools for cruising sailors: sight reduction, almanac data and fix computation.
why_it_matters: Scriptable sight reduction for a GNSS-free position fix.
hackathon_notes: Pure Python; combine with a camera-based star or sun altitude to automate a fix.

name: OpenCPN celestial navigation plugin
summary: OpenCPN plugin for entering sextant sights and plotting lines of position and fixes on the chart.
why_it_matters: Puts celestial fixes into a real chart plotter workflow.
hackathon_notes: Build against OpenCPN SDK; useful as UI reference.

name: SPEL Open Star Tracker
summary: Open star tracker software from the University of Chile space lab, flown on SUCHAI nanosatellites.
why_it_matters: Flight-tested open star tracker code, a basis for attitude from stars.
hackathon_notes: Python prototype; compare with tetra3/LOST.

name: Astrometry.net
summary: Blind astrometric solver that identifies star fields in arbitrary images and returns the precise sky pointing, using geometric hash indexes of star catalogs.
why_it_matters: Proven lost-in-space plate solving; with a known time and gravity vector it yields attitude and coarse position.
hackathon_notes: apt install astrometry.net plus index files for your field of view; solve-field on a night-sky photo.

name: Skyfield
summary: Python library for high-accuracy positions of stars, planets and Earth satellites, with proper time scales and reference frames.
why_it_matters: Gives the ephemerides any celestial or satellite-based nav prototype needs.
hackathon_notes: pip install skyfield; downloads ephemeris files on first use.

name: navalm
summary: Nautical almanac and celestial sight reduction for Unix/Linux with CLI, ncurses and web interfaces.
why_it_matters: Self-contained offline almanac, handy for air-gapped demos.
hackathon_notes: Very new and small; verify outputs against a published almanac.

name: REVE
summary: Radar Ego Velocity Estimator: robust 3D ego-velocity from 4D mmWave radar Doppler point clouds, the front-end used by Doer's radar-inertial odometry.
why_it_matters: Radar velocity works in smoke, fog and darkness, a strong aid for GNSS-denied drones.
hackathon_notes: ROS1; run on the provided datasets, pairs with christopherdoer/rio.

name: Yeti radar odometry
summary: Radar odometry for Navtech spinning radar that compensates motion distortion and Doppler effects.
why_it_matters: Shows the corrections needed to make scanning radar odometry accurate.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained; evaluated on Oxford Radar RobotCar.

name: STEAM-ICP
summary: Continuous-time lidar, radar, lidar-inertial and radar-inertial odometry built on the STEAM library.
why_it_matters: Ready continuous-time radar odometry pipeline evaluated on Boreas.
hackathon_notes: Docker build; test on Boreas sequences.

name: HKUST 4D Radar-Inertial Odometry
summary: Optimization-based, point-uncertainty-aware radar-inertial odometry for 4D radar.
why_it_matters: Sliding-window alternative to EKF radar-inertial methods.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 build; run on public 4D radar datasets.

name: ETH Radar-Inertial Odometry
summary: Graph-based, sparse radar-inertial odometry estimation from ETH ASL, using GTSAM.
why_it_matters: Factor-graph radar-inertial baseline for drones in degraded visual environments.
hackathon_notes: ROS build; datasets linked in README.

name: RINO
summary: Radar-inertial odometry for scanning radar targeting accuracy and robustness (T-ASE 2025).
why_it_matters: Recent scanning-radar inertial method to benchmark against.
hackathon_notes: Research code; check dataset requirements.

name: ORORA
summary: Outlier-robust radar odometry using graduated non-convexity-style estimation on radar feature correspondences (ICRA 2023).
why_it_matters: Robust estimation is what keeps radar odometry stable amid clutter and multipath.
hackathon_notes: Evaluated on MulRan and Oxford Radar; ROS build.

name: TBV Radar SLAM
summary: Radar SLAM with verified loop closures built on CFEAR radar odometry.
why_it_matters: Full radar-only SLAM, including loop closure, for long GNSS-denied drives.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 + Docker; pairs with CFEAR.

name: ReFeree
summary: Lightweight radar global descriptor for radar place recognition (RA-L 2024).
why_it_matters: Cheap loop-closure and relocalization for radar-only navigation.
hackathon_notes: Small codebase; test on MulRan/Oxford Radar.

name: Open-RadVLAD
summary: Fast radar place recognition using VLAD-style aggregation over radar polar scans.
why_it_matters: Simple radar relocalization baseline.
hackathon_notes: Evaluate on Oxford Radar RobotCar.

name: K-Radar
summary: 4D radar dataset and benchmark for object detection in diverse weather, with raw 4D tensors, lidar, cameras and GNSS.
why_it_matters: Bad-weather 4D radar data, also usable for radar odometry and perception experiments.
hackathon_notes: Very large dataset; request access and use subsets.

name: RadarHD
summary: Learns to generate high-resolution, lidar-like point clouds from low-cost single-chip mmWave radar.
why_it_matters: Makes cheap radar usable for mapping and localization in smoke or darkness.
hackathon_notes: Pretrained model and data provided; GPU needed.

name: pylgrim
summary: GNSS software receiver written in Python for learning acquisition, tracking and positioning.
why_it_matters: Python-readable receiver chain for teaching and quick experiments.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained since 2020; use for learning.

name: GNSS-DSP-tools
summary: Python code generators, acquisition and tracking for many GNSS signals (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, NavIC and more) operating on IQ recordings.
why_it_matters: Broadest signal coverage among lightweight SDR toolkits; quick to test a new recording.
hackathon_notes: Run acquire-*.py on an IQ file from any SDR; no build needed.

name: GNSS-matlab
summary: MATLAB code to generate GNSS PRN and secondary codes, dataless signals and spectra, with real captures.
why_it_matters: Reference signal generation for interference and receiver studies.
hackathon_notes: Old but self-contained; MATLAB needed.

name: TRN particle filter examples
summary: MATLAB particle filtering examples for terrain-referenced navigation, comparing standard, auxiliary, mixture and out-of-sequence measurement particle filters (accompanies an IEEE TAES 2018 paper).
why_it_matters: Directly addresses the ambiguous-terrain problem that breaks naive TRN.
hackathon_notes: Runs in MATLAB with simulated terrain; port the update logic to Python for a DEM demo.

name: Deep-TERNALOC
summary: Deep-learning-based terrain-referenced navigation and localization project from ITU Aerospace Research Center, with particle filter baselines.
why_it_matters: Learning-based TRN reference from an aerospace lab.
hackathon_notes: Partial code; read with the project website.

name: FederNet
summary: Terrain relative navigation for planetary landing that detects craters with a Mask R-CNN and matches them to a catalog using projective invariants.
why_it_matters: Crater-based TRN, the space analogue of map-matching navigation.
hackathon_notes: Thesis code; TensorFlow 2 and pretrained weights needed.

name: ESVIO
summary: Event-based stereo visual-inertial odometry combining stereo event and image streams with IMU (RA-L/IROS 2023).
why_it_matters: Event cameras keep tracking under fast motion and HDR where frame VIO fails.
hackathon_notes: ROS1; run on provided event datasets.

name: EKLT
summary: Asynchronous photometric feature tracking that combines events and frames (IJCV 2019).
why_it_matters: Feature tracks with very low latency, a front-end for event VIO.
hackathon_notes: Old ROS1 code; use for reference.

name: EMVS
summary: Event-based multi-view stereo: semi-dense 3D reconstruction from a moving event camera with known poses (IJCV 2018).
why_it_matters: Mapping from event cameras for depth in HDR scenes.
hackathon_notes: ROS1; reference implementation.

name: DEVO
summary: Deep Event Visual Odometry: learned monocular event-only VO trained on simulated events, generalizing to real benchmarks (3DV 2024).
why_it_matters: Event-only odometry without frames, useful at night or under strobing light.
hackathon_notes: PyTorch + CUDA; pretrained checkpoint available.

name: rpg_dvs_ros
summary: ROS drivers and tools for DVS/DAVIS event cameras, including calibration and rendering.
why_it_matters: Standard way to get event-camera data into ROS 1.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 only; for ROS 2 look at vendor drivers.

name: OpenEB
summary: Prophesee's open SDK for event-based vision: camera drivers, data formats, visualization and algorithm building blocks.
why_it_matters: Entry point for the most common commercial event sensors.
hackathon_notes: Build from source or packages; sample recordings available without hardware.

name: Tonic
summary: Python library for event-based datasets and transforms, in the style of torchvision.
why_it_matters: Fast access to many event datasets for learning-based event navigation.
hackathon_notes: pip install tonic; use transforms to voxel grids.

name: v2e
summary: Converts conventional video into realistic synthetic DVS event streams with sensor noise modeling.
why_it_matters: Lets you produce event data for training/testing without owning an event camera.
hackathon_notes: pip install; feed it drone footage to create event sequences.

name: E2VID
summary: Reconstructs intensity video from event streams with a recurrent network, enabling frame-based methods on event data.
why_it_matters: Bridge that lets standard VO/feature pipelines consume event camera data.
hackathon_notes: Pretrained model; PyTorch.

name: Event feature tracking (EM-ICP)
summary: MATLAB implementations of event-based feature tracking methods from the Penn GRASP lab.
why_it_matters: Reference algorithms for event-based VIO front-ends.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB; pair with MVSEC data.

name: LoranC receiver
summary: DSP-based Loran-C receiver project also aimed at the Russian Chayka chain, covering pulse detection and signal tracking.
why_it_matters: One of very few open receivers for low-frequency hyperbolic navigation, the basis of eLoran.
hackathon_notes: Old code from 2014; use for algorithm reference with recorded LF IQ data.

name: Loran-C reference signal generator
summary: NumPy API that generates Loran-C master and secondary station pulse groups with phase codes for simulation (Korean docs).
why_it_matters: Synthetic Loran/eLoran signals for testing receivers without LF hardware.
hackathon_notes: Small; translate README; combine with a tracking loop for a toy eLoran receiver.

name: torch2trt
summary: Converts PyTorch models to TensorRT engines with a single call, aimed at Jetson deployment.
why_it_matters: Simplest path to fast onboard inference for learned nav models.
hackathon_notes: Install on a Jetson with JetPack; not every layer converts - check supported ops.

name: Hello AI World (jetson-inference)
summary: NVIDIA's guide and library for deploying detection, segmentation and depth networks with TensorRT on Jetson, with camera streaming.
why_it_matters: Get onboard perception running on a Jetson in hours.
hackathon_notes: Use the Docker container; works with CSI/USB cameras.

name: jetson-containers
summary: Build system and prebuilt containers for ML on Jetson (PyTorch, ROS, LLMs, VLMs) matched to JetPack versions.
why_it_matters: Avoids the dependency hell of getting ROS and PyTorch onto a Jetson.
hackathon_notes: Use autotag to pull a container matching your JetPack.

name: ros_deep_learning
summary: ROS/ROS 2 nodes wrapping jetson-inference for detection, classification and segmentation with TensorRT.
why_it_matters: Drop-in onboard perception topics for a ROS robot on Jetson.
hackathon_notes: Build inside jetson-containers ROS image.

name: Isaac ROS nvblox
summary: GPU-accelerated 3D reconstruction (TSDF/ESDF) that provides Nav2 local costmaps from depth cameras.
why_it_matters: Real-time onboard mapping for obstacle avoidance without lidar.
hackathon_notes: Isaac ROS dev container; RealSense quickstart.

name: Isaac ROS DNN Inference
summary: ROS 2 packages for TensorRT and Triton inference on Jetson and x86, with encoder/decoder nodes for common model types.
why_it_matters: Standard ROS 2 path to run custom learned models onboard.
hackathon_notes: Use with an ONNX model; dev container required.

name: cuVSLAM
summary: NVIDIA's CUDA-accelerated visual odometry and SLAM library supporting mono to multi-camera rigs with optional IMU, with Python bindings.
why_it_matters: The engine behind Isaac ROS Visual SLAM, now usable directly from Python.
hackathon_notes: pip install the Python wheel on Jetson or x86 with CUDA; examples for EuRoC/KITTI.

name: LightGlue-ONNX
summary: ONNX export of SuperPoint/DISK + LightGlue feature matching with TensorRT and OpenVINO support.
why_it_matters: Fast learned matching on embedded hardware for visual geolocalization and VO.
hackathon_notes: Download prebuilt ONNX models; run with onnxruntime-gpu or TensorRT.

name: PINTO model zoo
summary: Large collection of models converted between TensorFlow, TFLite, ONNX, OpenVINO, TensorRT and others.
why_it_matters: Saves conversion time when a needed model must run on an edge accelerator.
hackathon_notes: Use the download scripts per model; check licences per model.

name: RKNN Model Zoo
summary: Rockchip's examples and converted models for its NPU (RK3588 and similar), with deployment code.
why_it_matters: Low-cost non-NVIDIA edge AI option common on small drones and UGVs.
hackathon_notes: Needs rknn-toolkit2 for conversion; run demos on an RK3588 board.

name: DepthAI
summary: Python API and examples for Luxonis OAK cameras, which run neural networks and stereo depth on the camera itself.
why_it_matters: Puts inference and depth on the sensor, freeing the companion computer.
hackathon_notes: pip install depthai; OAK-D required. Examples include spatial detection.

name: DepthAI ROS
summary: ROS 1/2 driver for Luxonis OAK cameras publishing depth, detections and IMU.
why_it_matters: Plug OAK cameras into a ROS nav stack.
hackathon_notes: Binary packages for major ROS 2 distros.

name: Hailo Raspberry Pi 5 examples
summary: Examples for Hailo-8/8L accelerators on Raspberry Pi 5 (AI Kit/HAT): detection, pose and segmentation pipelines; marked outdated in favor of hailo-apps.
why_it_matters: Cheapest route to real-time onboard inference on a Pi-based vehicle.
hackathon_notes: Repo points to hailo-ai/hailo-apps for current code; start there.
